name: prose-classic-one-liner
text: 58 yo M w/ HTN (on lisinopril 20), HLD (atorva 40), T2DM (A1c 7.2), active smoker 1 ppd, presents for f/u. BP today 142/88, BMI 31.2. Labs: TC 198, HDL 41, LDL 120, Cr 1.1
note: The clinic one-liner a resident actually types. Age and sex come from '58 yo M'; the A1c inside a parenthetical is not required, but nothing may be invented in its place.

name: prose-a1c-not-invented-from-bp
text:
Age: 58
Sex: M
BP today 142/88. A1c pending.
note: The A1c scan matched at most two digits, so '142/88' yielded a plausible-looking A1c of 14 - which would silently switch the calculator to the enhanced model.

name: prose-74-year-old-woman
text: 74-year-old woman with CKD. BP 128/74. BMI 24.8. Total cholesterol 210, HDL 62. eGFR 41. Never smoker.
note: Hyphenated age and a spelled-out sex.

name: prose-compact-age-sex
text: 58yo F, nonsmoker, BP 118/70, BMI 22.4, TC 180, HDL 70, eGFR 92
note: No space between the age and the marker.

name: prose-age-variants-yo-slash
text: 62 y/o male presenting for physical. BP 130/78

name: prose-pack-years-is-not-an-age
text:
Sex: Male
Social: 20 pack-years, quit 2010
BP 130/80
note: A bare 'years' must never supply an age, or every pack-year figure becomes one.

name: prose-labelled-age-beats-relatives-age
text:
Age: 58
Sex: Male
His 74-year-old mother has CKD
BP 130/80
note: A labelled age always wins, and the relative's age is not used.

name: prose-wife-has-diabetes
text:
Age: 58
Sex: Male
PMH: HTN
His wife has diabetes and he worries about it.
Problem List:
  Essential hypertension
BP 130/80
note: A relative followed by a VERB owns what comes next, not only a relative followed by a colon or dash.

name: prose-mother-with-t2dm
text:
Age: 49
Sex: Male
PMH: HTN, HLD. Mother with T2DM.
BP 130/80
note: 'Mother with T2DM' in a running PMH sentence is family history.

name: prose-patient-dx-survives-relative-mention
text:
Age: 58
Sex: Male
Problem List:
  Type 2 diabetes mellitus
His wife has diabetes too.
BP 130/80
note: Guarding the relative's mention must not erase the patient's own diagnosis.

name: prose-two-bps-triage-then-recheck
text: Age 62, male. Triage BP 158/94, recheck 142/86 after rest. BMI 29.1
note: The first reading is taken, consistent with how the dated reading lists are handled; the clinician can edit.

name: prose-quit-smoking-narrative
text:
Age: 60
Sex: Male
He quit smoking in 2015 after 30 pack-years. BP 134/80
note: A quit date makes this a former smoker.

name: prose-statin-intolerant
text:
Age: 60
Sex: Male
Statin-intolerant (myalgias with atorvastatin and rosuvastatin). BP 134/80
note: Intolerance is not current therapy, and the drug names in the parenthetical must not read as an active statin.

name: prose-labs-notable-for
text:
Age: 55
Sex: Female
Labs notable for TC 198, HDL 51, LDL 120, Cr 0.9, A1c 5.9
note: A comma-run of labs in a sentence.
